dialogues.speaker: Ami
dialogues.text: Why do people like to cook out in the open...?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Maybe because it's fun.

dialogues.speaker: Ami
dialogues.text: Is it really fun? What's so fun about cooking out in the open?

dialogues.speaker: Ami
dialogues.text: I don't get it.

dialogues.speaker: Ami
dialogues.text: And what if a bug falls into the pot? That's not fun at all...

dialogues.speaker: Ami
dialogues.text: That would be a pity, for the bug, also for the grown-ups who eat the food with the bug in it. It's not worth it at all.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Maybe it's because they have no choice...

dialogues.speaker: Ami
dialogues.text: What type of people can only cook outdoors? Is it because they don't have a home?

dialogues.speaker: Ami
dialogues.text: Then they really don't have a choice. That's sad.

dialogues.speaker: Ami
dialogues.text: But my dad has a home. Why does he still set up a fire and pot outside?

dialogues.speaker: Ami
dialogues.text: Is dad doing this for the homeless people?

dialogues.speaker: Ami
dialogues.text: Hmm... I think I get it now.

dialogues.speaker: Ami
dialogues.text: Wait, that's not right. Why does dad set up a fire and pot outside for himself, too?

dialogues.speaker: Ami
dialogues.text: I don't get it now!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: See you.

dialogues.speaker: Ami
dialogues.text: Hopefully there won't be any creepy-crawlies flying over again...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Just keep your eyes on the pot.

dialogues.speaker: Ami
dialogues.text: Do I need to keep watching until it's done?

dialogues.speaker: Ami
dialogues.text: Um... That actually makes sense. If you don't pay attention, bugs might fly in, or you might overcook it.

dialogues.speaker: Ami
dialogues.text: Ah, cooking is so complicated! Why doesn't everyone just eat fresh fruits? They are so sweet and delicious!

dialogues.speaker: Ami
dialogues.text: That way, no one has to cook or worry about bugs and overcooking!
